rules.what: purpose: the audience is freshers and engineers
old: - **Purpose:** walk a (possibly non-technical) user through the lifecycle one phase at a time.
new: walk a fresher or a working engineer through the lifecycle one phase at a time

rules.what: reads where the project stands through status.py
old: - **Reads:** `PRODUCT.md` (which sections are filled = how far along).
new: **Reads:** `STATUS.md` through `status.py route` (which phases are filled = how far along).

rules.what: writes no PRODUCT.md section; STATUS.md only via status.py on a yes
old: **Writes:** nothing itself — each phase skill writes its own section.
new: **Writes:** no `PRODUCT.md` section — each phase skill writes its own.
(`migrate --write`, `bypass`, `flag --order-override`), each on the user's yes.

rules.what: one status call first; it finds the first unfilled phase in the chain order
old: - **Run `python ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/tools/status.py next` first** (`MECHANISMS.md` §Status) and show its output. It finds the **first unfilled /
incomplete phase** in order: Vision → **Validate** → Scope → Plan → Architect → Structure → **Design (if UI)** →
new: status.py route` first — one call, nothing before it
It finds the **first unfilled / incomplete phase** in order: Vision → Validate (optional) → Scope → Plan → Architect → Structure → **Design (if UI)** →

rules.what: no STATUS.md: fresh -> /vision, old header -> migrate dry run then --write on yes, code -> /adopt (skill)
old: - **No `STATUS.md`:** no `PRODUCT.md` either → a fresh start, the next phase is **`/vision`**. A `PRODUCT.md` with
the old `_Last updated: … Stage:` header → offer `status.py migrate` (a dry run; `--write` only on the user's
yes) before anything else. Existing code with no `PRODUCT.md` → route to `/adopt` (below).
new: a fresh folder → **`/vision`**
existing code or a `PRODUCT.md`
old `_Last updated: … Stage:` header → `status.py migrate` (a dry run; `--write` only on the user's yes)

rules.what: no STATUS.md: the same routing decided in code
new: Next: /vision
Next: /adopt
Next: status.py migrate (a dry run)
migrate --write only on their yes

rules.what: report what the status command lists before proposing
old: - **Report what `next` lists, before proposing anything** — one line each, in plain words:
new: **Report what `route` lists, before proposing anything** — one line each, in plain words:

rules.what: a recorded order override is printed, never re-asked
old: (`status.py flag --order-override "<the user's reason>"`); `next` prints it — **do not re-ask**.
new: (`status.py flag --order-override "<the user's reason>"`); `route` prints it — **do not re-ask**.

rules.what: brownfield routes to /adopt; entering at /architect or /build stays offered but re-guesses the spine
old: - **Brownfield (existing code, no `PRODUCT.md`): route to `/adopt`.** It drafts an INFERRED `PRODUCT.md`
from what the repo actually contains and confirms it with the owner — after which orienting works
normally. Entering straight at `/architect` or `/build` still works and stays offered, but it leaves the
project with no spine, so every later phase re-guesses it.
new: which drafts or confirms the spine with the owner
entering straight at `/architect` or `/build` still works and stays offered, but every later phase then re-guesses the spine

rules.what: the map: one screen, shown on a first visit only (was: once, briefly, plain language); since 2.0 the list itself is route's (one source, P41)
old: ## Step 1 — Explain the map (once, briefly, plain language)
Show the journey in one screen so the user has the mental model:
new: ## Step 1 — Explain the map (only when `route` prints `Map: show it`)
`Map: skip it` → no map
Show `route`'s `Skills, in order` lines as printed (one source: never re-type the list) so the user has the mental model

rules.what: the map's later steps and /drift-check anytime: in route's skill list (SKILL_MAP) since 2.0
old: `#Architecture` chose) · `test` · `eval` · `ship` · `learn` · `/drift-check` anytime. Note: each step asks a few
questions and ends with a check before moving on — you stay in control.
new: /test -> /eval -> /ship -> /learn
/drift-check (are we still building the vision?)

rules.what: each step asks and ends with a check: you stay in control
new: questions and ends with a check before moving on — you stay in control.

rules.what: tell the next phase in plain language: what and why now
old: ## Step 2 — Run the next phase (one at a time)
1. Tell the user the next phase in plain language: *what it does and why it matters now.*
new: ## Step 2 — Offer the next phase, then run it (one phase per conversation)
the next phase in plain language — *what it does and why it matters now*

rules.what: every offer states the phase's length (now its size, from status.py) and the start-with-room warning; no price
old: - **Say how long a sitting it is, and when to start it** — on every offer, one phase or a batch; after a
phase's row in §Sitting lengths below with the version it was measured on: *"`/<phase>` takes <its row,
as written>: the agent's working time on playbook <version>, plus your own time answering and
reviewing."* A row that reads `not measured yet` is said as exactly that, never estimated. Then: *"Start
it in a new conversation, with room left on your plan: a run a usage limit cuts off mid-review loses review steps."* No prices —
what a run costs depends on the user's plan.
new: its size from `route`'s `Size:`
Start it with room left on your plan: a run a usage limit cuts off mid-review loses review steps.
Never a number of minutes, never a price — what a run costs depends on the user's plan.

rules.what: the offer is the last item of the phase's What YOU do next; since 2.0 the phase's own printed handoff line, no second route call (L1)
old: phase, the offer is the last item of its *What YOU do next* (`MECHANISMS.md` §Plain-language close). Quote the
new: the offer is the last item of its *What YOU do next* (`MECHANISMS.md` §Plain-language close) — the `Open a NEW conversation and type: /<next>` line the phase's close printed, word for word

rules.what: a batch only when legal (derivation phases, an input phase splits it); the user chooses; a batch is long
old: - **Offer a batch when it is legal — and only then** (`MECHANISMS-ON-DEMAND.md` §Batch mode): the next
phase and the one after it are both `derivation` (`STATE-MODEL.md` §2d) with no `input` phase
between. *"Run `/foundation` alone, or `/foundation` + `/contracts` + `/tickets` as one batch? The batch
still stops where a phase asks you to confirm; one commit per phase, one review at the end."* An
`input` phase splits the batch (UI product: `structure` alone → `design-system` → batch the three).
The user's choice is a choice, not a default. **The batch's sitting is its phases' rows added up** —
*"at least"* when one reads `not measured yet` — so a batch of long phases is offered as the long sitting
it is, not only as legal; the start-with-room line goes with it.
new: **Offer a batch only when `route` prints `Batch: legal`** (`MECHANISMS-ON-DEMAND.md` §Batch mode)
*"Run `/foundation` alone, or `/foundation` + `/contracts` + `/tickets` as one batch? The batch still stops where a phase asks you to confirm; one commit per phase, one review at the end."*
A batch is long. The user's choice is a choice, not a default.

new: STATE-MODEL.md §2d derivation phases

rules.what: invoke the phase skill (now only on the user's yes)
old: 2. **Invoke that phase's skill** (e.g. run `/vision`). Let it ask its questions and do its work.
new: **Invoke that phase's skill only on the user's yes** (e.g. run `/vision`)
The phase asks its questions and does its work.

rules.what: pause at the exit gate; never advance past an unmet gate
old: 3. When that skill reaches its **exit gate**, surface the result and **pause** — confirm with the user
that it's right before continuing. **Never advance past an unmet gate.**
new: When it reaches its **exit gate**, surface the result and **pause** — confirm with the user that it's right before continuing. **Never advance past an unmet gate.**

rules.what: after the close: next phase in a new conversation; stop and resume anytime with /playbook
old: 4. On confirmation, point to the next phase and repeat. The user can stop anytime and resume later by
running `/playbook` again (it re-orients from `PRODUCT.md`).
new: **After the phase's close, this conversation is done.**
**Never invoke the next phase in this conversation**
The user can stop anytime and resume later by running `/playbook` again.

rules.what: handoff
old: proposed next skill, or just keep running `/playbook` and I'll walk you through."
new: proposed next skill, or just keep running `/playbook` in a new conversation and I'll walk you through."

rules.what: dev-check, test and eval stay next until their verdict is pass; /deploy is never next by itself
old: their verdict is `pass`.)*
new: their verdict is `pass`. `/deploy` is never the next phase by itself: it runs when a milestone needs a real URL, else `/test` follows `/dev-check`.

rules.what: UI projects: recommend /frontend-audit once, never a gate; UI: no says nothing about the UI suite
old: - **UI projects only — recommend the enforcement tool, never gate on it.** If `STATUS.md` says `UI: yes` and
the ticket rows already include UI work, say once that `/frontend-audit` mechanically checks that UI against
the laws `/design-system` set (real contrast computation, not an opinion). It is a **recommendation, not a
phase**: it writes no `PRODUCT.md` section, so the first-unfilled frontier must never look for one, and a
user who ignores it is not behind on anything. For a backend/API/CLI product (has-UI false) say nothing —
neither UI-suite skill exists for that user.
new: **UI projects only — recommend the enforcement tool, never gate on it.**
say once that `/frontend-audit` mechanically checks that UI against the laws `/design-system` set (real contrast computation, not an opinion).
A **recommendation, not a phase**: it writes no `PRODUCT.md` section, and a user who ignores it is not behind.
`UI: no` → say nothing about the UI suite.
